Anthropic.content:
# Anthropic

- Create an account at https://platform.claude.com/
- Go to https://platform.claude.com/settings/keys and get your api key
- You will need to set the following environment variable to your key or you can set it touser_provided for users to provide their own.

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=user_provided

- You can determine which models you would like to have available withANTHROPIC_MODELS.

ANTHROPIC_MODELS=claude-fable-5-1,claude-fable-5,claude-opus-5,claude-opus-4-8,claude-opus-4-7,claude-sonnet-5,claude-sonnet-4-6,claude-opus-4-6,claude-opus-4-20250514,claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219,claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022,claude-3-5-haiku-20241022

Notes:

- Claude Fable 5.1 and Fable 5 are included in LibreChat's default Anthropic model catalog. Fable/Mythos-class models use the modern Anthropic profile in LibreChat: 1M context, 128K max output, adaptive thinking, prompt caching, andthinkingDisplay support for summarized or omitted reasoning output. Fable 5.1 keeps Fable 5's $10 input and $50 output rates per million tokens, with $12.50 cache writes and $0.25 cache reads.
- Claude Opus 5 is available through direct Anthropic, Anthropic on Vertex AI, and AWS Bedrock. It has a 1M-token context window and 128K-token maximum output. Adaptive thinking is enabled unless explicitly disabled; when disabled, LibreChat limitsxhigh or max effort to high to keep requests valid.
- Claude Sonnet 5 is available through direct Anthropic, Anthropic on Vertex AI, and AWS Bedrock. LibreChat assigns it a 1M-token context window and 128K-token maximum output, uses adaptive thinking with summarized display when thinking is enabled, and sends an explicit disabled setting when a user turns thinking off.
- Native Anthropic prompt-cache controls and 1M-context detection evaluate the configured Claude model ID directly. Compatible Sonnet and Opus IDs at version 4.6 or later, including matching later-version IDs, retain those controls without waiting for an exact catalog entry. Unsupported models keep prompt-cache controls hidden in the Agent Builder.
- Anthropic endpoint supports all Shared Endpoint Settings via thelibrechat.yaml configuration file, including streamRate, headers, titleModel, titleMethod, titlePrompt, titlePromptTemplate, and titleEndpoint
- To configure Anthropic or an Anthropic-compatible gateway as a separate custom endpoint, useprovider: "anthropic".

## Vertex AI

LibreChat supports running Anthropic Claude models through Google Cloud Vertex AI. This is useful if you:

- Already have Google Cloud infrastructure
- Want to use your existing GCP billing and credentials
- Need to comply with regional data residency requirements

### Quick Setup (Environment Variables)

Set the following environment variables to enable Anthropic via Vertex AI:
# Enable Vertex AI mode for Anthropic
ANTHROPIC_USE_VERTEX=true

# Vertex AI region (optional, defaults to 'us-east5')
# Modern models such as Fable 5.1 and Opus 5 require global, us, or eu.
# Specific regions serve Sonnet 4.6 and earlier.
ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_REGION=global

# Path to Google service account key file (optional)
# If not specified, uses default path: api/data/auth.json
GOOGLE_SERVICE_KEY_FILE=/path/to/service-account.json

### Prerequisites

- Google Cloud Project with Vertex AI API enabled
- Service Account with the following roles:
- Vertex AI User (roles/aiplatform.user)
- OrVertex AI Administrator for full access

- Claude models enabled in your Vertex AI Model Garden
- Service Account Key (JSON file) downloaded and accessible to LibreChat

### Advanced Configuration

For model name mapping and advanced settings (similar to Azure OpenAI configuration), use thelibrechat.yaml file:
endpoints:
  anthropic:
    vertex:
      region: global
      models:
        claude-fable-5-1:
          deploymentName: claude-fable-5-1
        claude-opus-5:
          deploymentName: claude-opus-5
        claude-sonnet-5:
          deploymentName: claude-sonnet-5
        claude-3.5-haiku:
          deploymentName: claude-3-5-haiku@20241022

For detailed YAML configuration options, see Anthropic Vertex AI Configuration.

Anthropic.title: What Is Claude AI Good For? 15 Best Uses (2026)
Anthropic.description: Claude is the AI assistant from Anthropic, and in late 2026 it is one of the “big four” chatbots alongside ChatGPT, Gemini and Grok. ... Claude is made by Anthropic, a San Francisco AI company founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers.
Anthropic.content:
# What Is Claude AI Good For? 15 Best Uses, Models and Limits (2026)

Claude is the AI assistant from Anthropic, and in late 2026 it is one of the “big four” chatbots alongside ChatGPT, Gemini and Grok. But what is Claude actually good for, and when should you use something else?

In short, Claude is at its best with writing, coding, long documents and multi-step tasks. It has a huge 1M-token context window on every plan, the Claude Code agent for developers, Cowork for office tasks, and a careful, natural writing style. It is weaker if you want AI-generated photos or live social media data.

This guide covers the 15 things Claude does best with example prompts, what each plan unlocks, how it compares with ChatGPT, Gemini and Grok, its weak spots, and tips to get better answers.

TL;DR

- Best at: writing and editing, coding (Claude Code), long documents and research, data analysis, and agent tasks through Cowork.
- Models (Nov 2026): Fable 5.2 (most capable), Opus 5.5 (default for hard work), Sonnet 5.5 (fast all-rounder), Haiku 5.5 (cheapest, fastest). All support 1M context.
- Free plan covers chat, files, web search, voice, artifacts, Claude Design and custom visuals with Sonnet and Haiku.
- Paid ($20 Pro and up) adds Opus, Claude Code, Cowork, Research and Claude in Chrome.
- Not good for: photo or art generation, live X data, or unlimited heavy use on the cheapest plan.

## What Is Claude?

Claude is made by Anthropic, a San Francisco AI company founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers. You can use it on claude.ai, in the Claude Desktop app (Mac, Windows), on iPhone and Android, in Chrome, inside Microsoft 365 and Slack, and through the API for developers.

Anthropic focuses on safety and on work tasks. That shows in what Claude does well: it reads carefully, follows detailed instructions, explains its reasoning and is less likely to make things up when it does not know.

## 15 Things Claude Is Best At

### Writing and communication

- Editing your writing. “Edit this cover letter to sound confident but not arrogant. Keep it under 250 words and explain your main changes.”
- Drafting long-form content like reports, articles and proposals with a consistent voice.
- Matching a style. Paste three of your old emails and ask Claude to write new ones in the same tone.
- Tricky messages. “Help me reply to this client who is unhappy about a delay. Be honest, calm and offer two options.”

### Coding and technical work

- Writing and fixing code in almost any language, with explanations.
- Agentic coding with Claude Code: it reads your project, edits files, runs tests and makes commits. See our best Claude model for coding guide.
- Explaining unfamiliar code or error messages step by step.

### Reading, research and analysis

- Long documents. With up to 1M tokens of context, Claude can read whole books, long contracts or large codebases in one go. “Summarise this 300-page report and list every risk with page references.”
- Comparing documents. “What changed between version 1 and version 2 of this contract?”
- Research mode (paid): runs many web searches and writes a cited report.
- Data analysis. Upload a spreadsheet or CSV and get charts, trends and outliers, with interactive custom visuals in chat.

### Getting things done

- Multi-step tasks with Cowork: organise folders, turn receipts into an expense report, build a slide deck from notes. Read what Claude Cowork is.
- Making real files: Excel with working formulas, PowerPoint decks and Word documents.
- Designs and docs with Claude Design, Slides and Docs artifacts, even on the free plan.
- Learning and tutoring. “Teach me basic statistics over five short lessons, quiz me after each one.”

## Best Uses by Job

Who | Top Claude uses 
---|---
Students | Explaining topics, essay feedback, study plans, summarising readings 
Writers and bloggers | Editing, outlines, rewriting for tone, research summaries 
Developers | Claude Code, debugging, code review, documentation 
Marketers | Campaign copy, content calendars, competitor research, one-pagers 
Lawyers and analysts | Long document review, comparisons, clause extraction (always verify) 
Small business owners | Emails, policies, spreadsheets, proposals, customer replies 
Researchers | Paper summaries, literature comparisons, data analysis 
Managers | Meeting notes to action items, reports, decks, scheduled summaries 

## Which Claude Model to Use for What

Model | Best for | API price (input / output per 1M tokens) 
---|---|---
Fable 5.2 | The hardest reasoning and research jobs | $8 / $40 
Opus 5.5 | Complex writing, coding, analysis; the default in Claude Code | $4 / $20 
Sonnet 5.5 | Fast everyday work, good quality | $2 / $10 
Haiku 5.5 | Quick answers, simple tasks, high volume | From $0.10 / $0.50 

All four support a 1M-token context window and up to 128K output tokens. In the app, pick the model from the menu next to the message box. Developers can start with our Claude API key guide.

## What Each Plan Unlocks

Feature | Free | Pro ($20) | Max ($100) | Ultra ($200) 
---|---|---|---|---
Chat, files, web search, voice, memory | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes 
Artifacts, Claude Design, Slides, Docs | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes 
Sonnet and Haiku | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes 
Opus | No | Yes | Yes | Yes 
Fable | No | Usage credits only | Up to 50% of weekly limit | Up to 50% of weekly limit 
Claude Code, Cowork, Research, Claude in Chrome | No | Yes | Yes | Yes 
Usage | Limited | 1x | 5x Pro | 10x Pro weekly, no 5-hour limit (verified) 

Full breakdown: Claude Free vs Pro vs Max vs Ultra. Students and some new users can get paid access cheaper: see how to get Claude Pro free.

## Claude vs ChatGPT vs Gemini vs Grok

Task | Best pick | Why 
---|---|---
Long documents | Claude | 1M context on every plan 
Coding agents | Claude | Claude Code is a leading coding agent 
Natural writing and editing | Claude | Careful, less generic tone 
Image generation | ChatGPT or Gemini | Claude has no image model 
Voice conversations | ChatGPT | Most mature voice mode 
Google Workspace | Gemini | Built into Gmail, Docs and Drive 
Live X and news | Grok | Direct X search 
Office agent tasks | Claude | Cowork with files, browser and schedules 

Our detailed head-to-head: ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini vs Grok.

## What Claude Is Not Good For

- Photos and AI art: Claude cannot generate them. It makes charts, diagrams, SVGs and designs instead. Details in can Claude make images.
- Heavy daily use on Pro: limits reset every five hours and weekly. Chat, Claude Code and Cowork share the same pool.
- Live social media data: no built-in X or TikTok feed.
- Sometimes too careful: it may add caveats or decline borderline requests. Clear context usually fixes this.
- Facts after its training data: turn on web search for current events.
- Agreeing too easily: like all chatbots it can be agreeable. Our guide to stop Claude agreeing with everything helps.

## Tips to Get Better Results

- Give context: who you are, who the audience is, what “good” looks like.
- Use Projects to store files and standing instructions for recurring work.
- Ask for a plan first on big tasks: “Outline your approach before writing.”
- Use XML-style tags for long inputs: <report>…</report> helps Claude keep sections apart.
- Ask it to check itself: “Review your answer for errors and missing points.”
- Use Skills for repeat workflows. See our Claude Skills guide.
- Pick the right model: Haiku or Sonnet for quick tasks saves your limit for Opus jobs.

## How to Start in 5 Minutes

- Go to claude.ai or install the app, and sign up with email or Google.
- Ask a real task from your day, not a test question.
- Upload a document and ask for a summary with key action points.
- Try “draw this as a diagram” to see custom visuals.
- If you like it, try Pro for Opus, Claude Code and Cowork.

Step-by-step tour: how to use Claude AI.

## Privacy and Safety

- Check your data settings in Settings > Privacy, including whether chats can be used to improve models.
- Do not paste passwords, ID numbers or client secrets.
- For Cowork and Claude in Chrome, use a dedicated folder and avoid sensitive sites.
- Team and Enterprise plans add admin controls and stricter data terms for work use.

## My Take

If your work is mostly words, code or documents, Claude is often the best assistant you can use.

Its long context and careful writing make a real difference on serious work, and Claude Code plus Cowork turn it into a do-the-job tool rather than a chat window. Keep ChatGPT or Gemini around for images and voice, and Grok for live X news.

## FAQ

### What is Claude AI mainly used for?

Writing and editing, coding, reading long documents, research, data analysis and multi-step tasks like building reports and slide decks.

### Is Claude better than ChatGPT?

For long documents, coding and natural writing, many people prefer Claude. ChatGPT is stronger for images, voice and its larger app ecosystem.

### Is Claude free?

Yes, there is a free plan with Sonnet and Haiku, file uploads, web search, voice, artifacts and Claude Design. Opus, Claude Code and Cowork need a paid plan.

### Can Claude browse the internet?

Yes. Web search is on every plan, and paid plans add Research mode and Claude in Chrome for browsing tasks.

### Is Claude good for coding?

Yes. Claude Code is one of the most popular coding agents, and Opus 5.5 is its default model on paid plans.

### Can Claude read PDFs and spreadsheets?

Yes. Upload PDFs, Word, Excel or CSV files and ask questions, request summaries or get charts.

### What can’t Claude do?

It cannot generate photos or AI art, does not have live X data, and has usage limits that reset every five hours and weekly.

OpenAI.title: The provider & model landscape
OpenAI.description: OpenAI — the GPT family and the o-series. The widely used GPT models plus a line of "reasoning" models (the o-series) that spend extra compute thinking before answering. ... OpenAI's GPT and o-series (behind ChatGPT)...
OpenAI.content:
# The provider & model landscape

Key takeaways A handful of providers — Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta and several others ship the model families you'll actually use. The big split is proprietary vs open-weight — hosted frontier models you can't control, versus downloadable models you can run yourself. Choose on fit, not the leaderboard — capabilities converge and the "best" model changes constantly, so pick by ecosystem and need.

This is lesson 6 of the path, and the first of Module 2 — the map of who makes these models, what they cost, and how you reach them. The previous module was about how a model works on the inside; now we zoom out to the marketplace around it. By the end of this lesson you'll know the major providers and their flagship model families, the one dividing line that matters most (whose computer the model runs on), the routes that let you reach many models at once, and a sane way to think about a field that announces a new "best" model every few months.

One honest caveat up front, and it runs through this whole module: specifics here age fast. Model names, version numbers, prices and rankings change on a timescale of weeks. So this lesson names families rather than this-week's-release, and everything concrete is offered as a snapshot, not a fact to memorise. When you need a current figure, the only reliable source is the provider's own live documentation.

## The major providers and their families

A model family is a lineage of related models from one provider — usually offered in a few sizes and refreshed over time. Here are the families you'll meet most often, described neutrally.

- Anthropic — the Claude family. Reached through an API and through Anthropic's own apps and developer tools. Claude is known for coding, long-context work and following instructions carefully.
- OpenAI — the GPT family and the o-series. The widely used GPT models plus a line of "reasoning" models (the o-series) that spend extra compute thinking before answering. Many people first meet these through the ChatGPT consumer product, which is the app built on top of those models.
- Google — the Gemini family. Google's flagship multimodal models, available through its developer platform and consumer apps, and notable for large context windows and tight integration with Google's cloud.
- Meta — the Llama family. Meta's models are open-weight: you can download the weights and run them yourself. Llama has anchored much of the open ecosystem and the tooling built around it.

Beyond the largest players, several other providers ship capable families worth knowing by name:

- Mistral (France) — efficient models, including open-weight releases.
- DeepSeek (China) — models that drew attention for strong reasoning and coding at low cost, with open-weight releases.
- Alibaba — the Qwen family — a broad, frequently updated open-weight lineup.
- xAI — the Grok family — proprietary models tied to xAI's products.
- Cohere — models aimed at enterprise use cases like retrieval and search.

This list is not exhaustive and it will shift. Treat it as "the neighbourhoods of the city," not a ranking. No family here is uniformly best; each has releases that lead on some task and trail on others.

## The big dividing line: proprietary vs open-weight

If you remember one distinction from this lesson, make it this one. It shapes cost, privacy, control and capability more than any benchmark does.

Proprietary (hosted) models run on the provider's servers. You send your request to their API or use their app, the model runs on their hardware, and you get an answer back. You never possess the weights — the trained numbers that are the model. The frontier of capability almost always lives here, because training and serving these models takes enormous, expensive infrastructure. The trade-off: you depend on the provider for availability, pricing and policy, and your data leaves your machine to be processed.

Open-weight models publish their trained weights for download. You (or a host you trust) run them on your own hardware. This buys control and privacy — the model can run fully offline, your code never leaves your network, and no provider can change the price or retire the model out from under you. The costs are real too: the very best open-weight models typically trail the closed frontier by a step, and you need capable hardware (a strong GPU or a lot of memory) plus the know-how to run and update them.

A word on "open." Open-weight means you get the weights; it does not necessarily mean open-source in the full sense (training data and code, an OSI-approved licence). Some releases come with usage restrictions. Read the licence before you build on one.

Proprietary / hosted | Open-weight 
---|---
Where it runs | Provider's servers | Your hardware (or a host you choose) 
How you reach it | API or subscription | Download and self-host 
Capability | Usually leads the frontier | Often a step behind, closing fast 
Privacy / control | Data leaves your machine; provider sets terms | Runs offline; you control everything 
Cost shape | Pay per use or monthly fee | Hardware + electricity + your time 
Examples (illustrative) | Claude, GPT/o-series, Gemini, Grok | Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral releases 

For local, hands-on work — say, decoding sensitive radio captures with GopherTrunk on an air-gapped machine — an open-weight model you run yourself may matter more than a few points of capability. For the hardest novel problem at 2 a.m., a frontier hosted model often earns its keep. Many developers keep both within reach.

## Aggregators and cloud routes

You don't always go straight to a provider. Two kinds of intermediary let you reach many models through one door.

Aggregators sit in front of multiple providers and expose them through a single account and API. OpenRouter is the best-known example: one key, one billing relationship, and the ability to switch between dozens of models — proprietary and open-weight — by changing a single string in your request. That makes comparison and fallback easy, at the cost of adding a middleman between you and the provider.

Cloud platforms offer models inside the big cloud ecosystems, which is convenient if your project already lives there:

- AWS Bedrock — many model families, including third-party ones, served within Amazon's cloud.
- Google Vertex AI — Google's platform, the enterprise route to Gemini and other models.
- Azure — Microsoft's cloud, a common enterprise route to OpenAI's models and others.

The appeal of the cloud route is governance and integration: billing, security, data-residency and access controls handled the same way as the rest of your infrastructure. The trade-off is a bit more setup and sometimes a lag before the very newest model versions arrive, compared with going to the provider directly.

## How to think about a churning field

Every few months, someone ships a model that tops some chart, and the headlines declare a new king. It is genuinely hard to keep up — and mostly, you shouldn't try to. Three observations make the churn manageable.

Capabilities converge. When one provider unlocks a capability — longer context, better reasoning, tool use — the others tend to follow within a release or two. The frontier moves together. So the gap between "the best model" and "a very good model" is usually smaller than the marketing suggests, and it narrows further every quarter.

Leaderboards churn — and don't measure your work. A model can lead a public benchmark and still be a poor fit for your codebase, your latency budget, or your privacy rules. A leaderboard is a single number on someone else's test; your project is the only benchmark that counts. We'll look hard at reading benchmarks skeptically in the next lesson, Coding models compared.

So choose on fit and ecosystem, not on one score. The questions that actually decide it are durable: Which interface do I want to work in — an app, an IDE, the terminal? What's my budget? Do I need the model to run offline? Does it plug into the tools and cloud I already use? Those answers change slowly even as the models change fast. Pick a family and a route that fit your work, and treat swapping models as the cheap, routine operation it has become — especially if you go through an aggregator.

Quick check: what most clearly distinguishes an open-weight model from a proprietary one?

## Recap

- Provider families — Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's GPT and o-series (behind ChatGPT), Google's Gemini and Meta's open-weight Llama lead, alongside Mistral, DeepSeek, Qwen, Grok and Cohere.
- Proprietary vs open-weight — hosted frontier models you reach by API or subscription versus downloadable models you run yourself for control and privacy.
- Aggregators and cloud routes — OpenRouter and clouds like AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex and Azure let you reach many models through one account.
- Capabilities converge — the frontier moves together, so the gap between "best" and "very good" is smaller and shrinking.
- Choose on fit — pick by interface, budget, privacy and ecosystem, not by whichever model led a leaderboard this month.
- Specifics age fast — treat every model name, price and ranking here as a snapshot, and check the provider's live docs for current numbers.

Next up: the axes that actually tell coding models apart — and how to read a benchmark without being fooled by it — in Coding models compared.

OpenAI.content:
# GPT (OpenAI) - Original System Prompt Reference

## Overview

ChatGPT/GPT-5 system prompts have been leaked and documented. OpenAI also publishes prompting guides.

## Key Characteristics

- Tone: Helpful, warm, conversational, playful yet clear
- Personality: Multiple preset personalities (Efficient, Friendly, Nerd, etc.)
- Approach: Comprehensive, well-organized, steerable
- Philosophy: Reduced sycophancy (from GPT-5), reduced hallucinations
- Verbosity: Controllable through parameters and prompting

## Sources

### Official Guides

- https://cookbook.openai.com/examples/gpt-5/ (prompting guides)
- https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-1/ (release notes)

### Community Collections

- CL4R1T4S:OPENAI/ChatGPT5-*.mkd
- leaked-system-prompts: Various ChatGPT versions

## Notable Features (from documentation)

- GPT-5.1 "warmer by default and more conversational"
- Personality presets: Efficient, Friendly, Nerd, Cynic, Professional, Candid, Quirky
- Adaptive reasoning with controllable verbosity
- Granular style controls (conciseness, warmth, emoji usage)

## Adapted Versions

Seegpt_style_mini.md, gpt_style_standard.md, and gpt_style_complete.md for provider-agnostic adapted versions suitable for KOAssistant.

Model | Model ID ---|--- GPT 6 Luna | gpt-6-luna GPT 5.6 Sol | gpt-5.6-sol GPT 5.6 Terra | gpt-5.6-terra GPT 5.6 Luna | gpt-5.6-luna GPT 5.5 | gpt-5.5 GPT Instant (latest) | chat-latest GPT 5.4 | gpt-5.4 GPT 5.4 Mini | gpt-5.4-mini GPT 5.2 | gpt-5.2 GPT 5 | gpt-5 GPT 5 Mini | gpt-5-mini GPT 5 Nano | gpt-5-nano GPT 4.1 | gpt-4.1 GPT 4.1 Mini | gpt-4.1-mini GPT 4o | gpt-4o GPT 4o Mini | gpt-4o-mini GPT Realtime Cluster | gpt-realtime-2025-08-28 GPT Realtime Mini | gpt-realtime-mini-2025-12-15 GPT Realtime 2 | gpt-realtime-2 o3 | o3 You can also setmodel.temperature from 0 to 2. If omitted, Vapi uses 0.5. ### Regional models To keep model requests in one region, setmodel.model to a region-qualified model ID. The value after the colon is the Azure region that serves the request. You can also select these IDs in the model picker for assistants, squads, evals, and structured outputs. curl -X PATCH "https://api.vapi.ai/assistant/ASSISTANT_ID" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $VAPI_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": { "provider": "openai", "model": "gpt-5.4:eastus2" } }' If you've added an Azure OpenAI credential for the selected region, Vapi routes the request through it. Otherwise, Vapi uses its own deployment in that region. A region-qualified request never falls back to another region. # Gemini Models Reference

Detailed information about available Gemini models (as of September 2026; speech models added 2026-09-24).

## Model Comparison

### Gemini 3.8 — Frontier Flash (GA, current default)

#### gemini-3.8-flash

Status: Generally available (released September 2, 2026) Alias:flash (the current default Flash)

Strengths:

- Google's "most intelligent Flash model", positioned for long-horizon software engineering, autonomous agents, and multi-step enterprise work
- Vs 3.7 Flash (Google's own numbers): Terminal-Bench 2.1 90.8% vs 81.6%, SWE-Bench Pro 61.6% vs 60.4%, SWE-Atlas 51.9% vs 48.0%, τ³-bench Banking 38.1% vs 30.9%, CharXiv 86.2% vs 84.5%; HLE-Verified 54.9%
- Humanity's Last Exam is flat (45.4% vs 45.7%) — the gains are agentic and tool-use, not open-ended reasoning
- Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index: 57 atmedium (3.7 Flash 56,
3.6 Flash 52); ~310 output tok/sec
- Prompt-injection robustness improved (Gray Swan); CBRN and cyber-offense safeguards carried forward

Specifications:

- Context window: 1,048,576 tokens input / 65,536 tokens output
- Multimodal input: text, image, video, audio, PDF; text output only
- thinking_level: low, medium (default), high. minimal is not
supported and returns HTTP 400 ("Thinking level MINIMAL is not supported
for this model", verified 2026-09-03). The client downgrades minimal to
low on this model.
- Google's release note: the model "works harder" on complex tasks — extra reasoning steps, iterative tool calls — so higher effort levels cost more tokens. Measured 2026-09-03:low spent 0 thinking tokens on a one-word
reply; the default medium spent 79.
- Supports caching, code execution, computer use (preview), file search, function calling, Maps and Search grounding, structured outputs, URL context, Batch / Flex / Priority inference. No audio generation, image generation, or Live API.
- Google's migration notes for the 3.x line:thinking_budget is gone
(use thinking_level); temperature / top_p / top_k /
candidate_count are deprecated sampling params on this model.

Best for:

- Default Flash / sub-agent-delegation choice for most tasks
- Agentic coding loops, terminal automation, multi-file projects
- Finance/legal agent workflows (Vals Finance Agent V2, Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark lead their Flash class)

Pricing:

- Input: $0.75 / 1M tokens through 2026-12-31; $1.50 from 2027-01-01
- Output: $3.75 / 1M tokens through 2026-12-31; $7.50 from 2027-01-01 (includes thinking tokens)
- Context caching $0.075 → $0.15; Batch 50% off
- 1M context window at base price (no surcharge tier)

Shipped alongsidegemini-3.8-flash-cyber — vulnerability discovery and
patching (>70% on Google's internal 20-language vuln benchmark, 47.2% pass@1
on CWE-Bench patching). Access is limited to Google's Fairwind Program
(government authorities, critical-infrastructure operators, software
maintainers), so this client cannot alias it.

### Gemini 3.7 — Prior Frontier Flash (GA)

#### gemini-3.7-flash

Status: Generally available (released August 13, 2026) Alias:flash-3.7 (was flash for three weeks until 3.8 shipped)

Strengths:

- The coding jump in the 3.x Flash line: DeepSWE v1.1 65.3% vs 49.0% on 3.6 Flash, FrontierCode 1.1 43.6% vs 34.4%, AutomationBench 30.4% vs 17.0%, WebDev Arena Elo 1588 vs 1538
- Terminal-Bench 2.1 85.8%, OSWorld-2.0 47.9%, GDM-MRCR v2 (128k) 97.0%
- Google keeps it "fully supported for efficiency-first workloads". Measured 2026-09-03 on a one-word prompt, though,low on 3.7 still spent 45–88
thinking tokens where low on 3.8 spent 0, and a max_output_tokens=50
call at low hit MAX_TOKENS. Budget output generously on this model.

Specifications:

- Context window: 1,048,576 tokens input / 65,536 tokens output
- Multimodal input: text, image, video, audio, PDF
- thinking_level: low, medium (default), high; minimal returns
HTTP 400 (verified 2026-09-03), same as 3.8

Pricing:

- Same schedule as 3.8: $0.75 / $3.75 through 2026-12-31, then $1.50 / $7.50

### Gemini 3.6 — Older Flash (GA)

#### gemini-3.6-flash

Status: Generally available (released July 21, 2026) Alias:flash-3.6 (was flash until 3.7 shipped)

Strengths:

- Builds on 3.5 Flash for coding, knowledge work, and multimodal tasks
- The last Flash that acceptsthinking_level='minimal' (verified
2026-09-03) — pin here for true no-thinking transcription/extraction
- ~17% fewer output tokens than 3.5 Flash on the Artificial Analysis index (the headline efficiency win — addresses 3.5's verbosity)
- Quality gains alongside efficiency: DeepSWE 49% vs 37%, MLE-Bench 63.9% vs 49.7%, OSWorld-Verified 83.0% vs 78.4%, GDPval-AA v2 1421 vs 1349
- Built-in client-side Computer Use tool via the Gemini API (Preview)
- Dynamic thinking on by default (configurable viathinking_level)

Specifications:

- Context window: ~1M tokens input / 65,536 tokens output
- Multimodal: text, image, audio, video
- Defaultthinking_level: medium — set explicitly to minimal for
transcription/classification/extraction or the model will silently spend
output tokens on reasoning
- Enhanced Frontier Safety safeguards (CBRN, cyber-offense); model card notes a slight tone regression vs 3.5 Flash

Best for:

- Pinning prior-gen behavior, andminimal-thinking bulk work
- Cost-sensitive high-volume agentic work (cheaper output than 3.5)

Pricing:

- Same schedule as 3.7 and 3.8 on Google's pricing page (fetched 2026-09-03): $0.75 / $3.75 through 2026-12-31, then $1.50 / $7.50. The July table here said $1.50 / $7.50 flat; the intro rate now covers all three.
- 1M context window at base price (no surcharge tier)

Shipped alongside two sibling models, neither wired into this client's alias table:

- gemini-3.5-flash-lite — GA. Fastest 3.5-class model (350 output tok/sec),
$0.30 / $2.50. This is now the lite alias target (repointed 2026-07-21
from gemini-2.5-flash-lite). It costs ~6x more on output than the 2.5 model it
replaces; that was accepted deliberately — the 2.5 generation is retired
regardless of price.
- gemini-3.5-flash-cyber — vuln-finding, fine-tuned on 3.5 Flash; powers
CodeMender. NOT generally available: access is limited to governments
and trusted partners under a pilot program due to dual-use risk. It cannot
simply be added as an alias.

### Gemini 3.5 — Legacy Flash (GA)

#### gemini-3.5-flash

Status: Generally available (released May 19, 2026 at Google I/O); Google's model list now labels it "legacy". No shutdown date. Alias:flash-3.5 (was flash until 3.6 shipped)

Strengths:

- Frontier-class performance — beats Gemini 3.1 Pro on most coding and agentic benchmarks
- Runs ~4× faster on output tokens than other frontier models
- Frontier intelligence at sub-Pro pricing
- Dynamic thinking on by default (configurable viathinking_level)

Specifications:

- Context window: ~1M tokens input
- Multimodal: text, image, audio, video
- Knowledge cutoff: January 2026
- Defaultthinking_level: medium (was high on prior 3.x — set
explicitly to minimal for transcription/classification/extraction or
the model will silently spend output tokens on reasoning)

Best for:

- Pinning to prior-gen Flash behavior when 3.6–3.8 output differs
- Agentic coding loops, terminal automation, multi-file projects
- Multimodal document analysis where structure must be preserved

Pricing:

- Input: $1.50 / 1M tokens
- Output: $9.00 / 1M tokens
- 1M context window at base price (no surcharge tier)

### Gemini 3.x — Prior Preview Generation

#### gemini-3-flash-preview

Status: Preview (still callable — kept for back compat) Alias:flash-3

The previous-generation Flash. Use when you need to pin behavior established before the 3.5 cutover. Google's deprecation page lists gemini-3.6-flash as its replacement, with no shutdown date. New code should targetflash (gemini-3.8-flash) instead.

Pricing:

- Input: $0.30 / 1M tokens
- Output: $2.50 / 1M tokens

#### gemini-3.1-pro-preview

Status: Preview. DEPRECATED from routing 2026-09-03 (Oskar): "its Pareto efficiency is too poor compared to the later Flash models." At today's rates it costs 2.7× the input and 3.2× the output of 3.8 Flash (1.3× / 1.6× once the Flash intro pricing ends), and 3.5 Flash already beat it on most coding and agentic benchmarks. The ID stays callable for pinned code. Alias: none —pro now resolves to gemini-3.8-flash. For maximum
reasoning use Flash with thinking_level='high'.

Strengths:

- Was the most capable Gemini Pro in the API
- 1M context with tiered pricing above 200K

Specifications:

- Context window: ~1M tokens input
- Long context surcharge: 2× above 200K input tokens
- Multimodal: text, image, video, audio

Best for:

- Nothing in new code. Pinned callers only.

Pricing:

- Input: $2.00 / 1M tokens (≤200K), $4.00 (>200K)
- Output: $12.00 / 1M tokens (≤200K), $18.00 (>200K) — the July table here said $24.00; Google's pricing page says $18.00 (fetched 2026-09-03)

Note: Google announcedgemini-3.5-pro at I/O on 2026-05-19 for June.
As of 2026-09-03 it is not in the API model list or on the pricing page;
DeepMind still lists it as "coming soon". When it ships it gets the same
price/quality test against the current Flash before any alias points at it.

### Gemini 2.5 — DEPRECATED (retired 2026-07-21)

⚠️ The Gemini 2.5 text generation is retired from routing. A 2025-era generation; the cost saving does not justify the quality gap. Model IDs remain callable so pinned code does not hard-break, but do not target them in new work. Thelite alias now resolves to gemini-3.5-flash-lite.

#### gemini-2.5-flash

Status: Stable, generally available Alias:stable-flash

Strengths:

- Production stability without preview-tier volatility
- Solid price-performance for reasoning tasks
- Empirically token-perfect on dense transcription benchmarks (May 2026)

Specifications:

- Context window: ~1M tokens input
- Multimodal: text, image, video, audio

Best for:

- Production workloads where preview models are too volatile
- High-volume tasks with a quality floor
- Multimodal extraction when cost matters

# Gemini (Google) - Original System Prompt Reference

## Overview

Gemini's system prompts reflect Google's safety-focused, professional AI design philosophy.

## Key Characteristics

- Tone: Professional, formal, neutral, buttoned-up
- Approach: Safety-prioritized, reliable, accountable
- Information: Balanced viewpoints, evidence-citing, neutral framing
- Personality: Deliberately limited to manage expectations
- Consistency: Steady, predictable responses

## Sources

### Community Collections

- CL4R1T4S:GOOGLE/Gemini-2.5-Pro-*.md
- Various dated versions available

## Notable Features (from research)

- "Does not have personal views, beliefs, or the ability to form opinions"
- Frames issues neutrally, presents balanced viewpoints
- Professional persona as part of safety framework
- Higher emotional stability, lower agreeableness than humans
- Gemini Live has more natural conversation features

## Design Philosophy

Google DeepMind prioritizes safety and reliability over conversational warmth. The formal tone reduces the risk of inappropriate responses while maintaining clear boundaries.

## Adapted Versions

Seegemini_style_mini.md, gemini_style_standard.md, and gemini_style_complete.md for provider-agnostic adapted versions suitable for KOAssistant.

Google.content:
# Invoking Gemini

Delegate tasks to Google's Gemini models when they offer advantages over Claude.

## When to Use Gemini

Image generation:

- Blog header images, illustrations, diagrams
- Style-guided image creation (risograph, editorial, etc.)
- Text rendering in images

Speech (TTS):

- Narration, voice-over, read-aloud with style direction per line
- A custom voice designed from a written description
- Two-speaker dialogue

Structured outputs:

- JSON Schema validation with property ordering guarantees
- Pydantic model compliance
- Strict schema adherence (enum values, required fields)

Cost optimization:

- Parallel batch processing (Gemini 3 Flash is lightweight)
- High-volume simple tasks

Multi-modal tasks:

- Image analysis with JSON output
- Video processing
- Audio transcription with structure

## Setup
uv pip install requests pydantic

Credentials — Option A (recommended): Cloudflare AI Gateway

Source/mnt/project/proxy.env with CF_ACCOUNT_ID, CF_GATEWAY_ID, CF_API_TOKEN.
Requests route through Cloudflare AI Gateway, bypassing IP blocks. Google API key stored in gateway via BYOK.

Credentials — Option B: Direct Google API

If noproxy.env, falls back to direct: GOOGLE_API_KEY.txt or API_CREDENTIALS.json.

## Image Generation

Generate images using Gemini's native image models. This is the primary way to create illustrations, blog headers, diagrams, and visual content.

### Quick Start
import sys
sys.path.append('/mnt/skills/user/invoking-gemini/scripts')
from gemini_client import generate_image

# One call — returns {"path": "...", "caption": "..."} or None
result = generate_image("A watercolor painting of a mountain lake at sunset")
print(result["path"])  # /mnt/user-data/outputs/gemini_image_1740000000.png

### Function Signature
generate_image(
    prompt: str,                    # The image description
    output_path: str = None,        # Auto-generates if omitted
    model: str = "nano-banana-2",   # Default: fast. Use "image-pro" for quality
    temperature: float = 0.7,       # 0.5-0.7 for diagrams, 0.7-0.8 for illustrations
) -> dict | None
# Returns: {"path": "/mnt/user-data/outputs/gemini_image_*.png", "caption": str|None}
# Returns None on failure

### Model Selection

Alias | Model | Best For | Cost/image 
---|---|---|---
"nano-banana-2" or "image" | gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview | Fast iteration, drafts | $0.067 
"image-pro" or "nano-banana-pro" | gemini-3-pro-image-preview | Published content, text rendering | $0.134 

### Complete Blog Header Example
import sys
sys.path.append('/mnt/skills/user/invoking-gemini/scripts')
from gemini_client import generate_image

# 1. Compose prompt with style prefix + subject
style_prefix = (
    "Style: Risograph-inspired editorial illustration. "
    "Visible halftone dot texture and slight color misregistration between layers. "
    "Limited ink palette: deep indigo, warm coral, and sage green on off-white paper. "
    "Layered transparency where colors overlap creates rich secondary tones. "
    "Modern and professional — the aesthetic of an indie design studio, not a fantasy novel. "
    "Generous whitespace. No photorealism, no glow effects, no cyberpunk. No text or labels."
)
subject = "A raven perched on a stack of books, observing a network graph"
prompt = f"{style_prefix}\n\nSubject: {subject}. Wide landscape format, suitable as a blog header."

# 2. Generate (use image-pro for published content)
result = generate_image(prompt, model="image-pro", temperature=0.75)

if result:
    print(f"Saved: {result['path']}")
    # 3. Present to user
    # present_files([result["path"]])

### Prompt Patterns

- Style prefix + subject: Prepend a style description, then describe the subject
- Be specific about style: "Risograph-inspired editorial illustration" not "a nice picture"
- Include composition: "Wide landscape format" / "centered, high contrast"
- Text rendering: "A poster with the text 'SALE' in bold red letters" (works well with image-pro)
- Negative constraints: "No photorealism, no glow effects" to avoid defaults

### Custom Output Path
result = generate_image(
    "A logo for a coffee shop called 'Bean There'",
    output_path="/mnt/user-data/outputs/coffee_logo.png"
)

## Speech Generation (TTS)

Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Flash-Lite TTS went GA on 2026-09-23. Output is WAV, 24 kHz mono 16-bit, SynthID-watermarked.
from gemini_client import generate_speech, design_voice, list_voices

r = generate_speech("Odin kept two ravens. <short pause> Huginn was thought.",
                    output_path="/tmp/line.wav", voice="Algenib",
                    style="quiet and dry, unhurried")
# {'path': '/tmp/line.wav', 'seconds': 4.2, 'audio_tokens': 135} or None

v = design_voice("A low, dry, quietly amused male voice with a faint rasp. "
                 "Soft southern British accent.", "narrator", gender="male",
                 language_code="en-GB")      # {'id': 'voice_...', 'sample_path': ...}
generate_speech("...", voice=v["id"])

lows = list_voices(gender="male", pitch="low")   # library of 2,089 prebuilt voices

- Voices: 30 studio voices (Charon, Kore, Algenib "gravelly",
Enceladus "breathy", ...) plus 2,059 persona voices with ids like
en-gb-storyteller-4. list_voices() returns accent, pitch, gender and a
description for each; the accent filter needs the exact string ("Winchester
English"), so filter accents on the returned field.
- Style: passstyle= (a speech_metadata annotation). Do not prefix the
text with "Style: ..." — the 3.8 models read the prefix aloud, and
systemInstruction is rejected. Inline events go in the text: <laugh>,
<sigh>, <breath>, <short pause>; CAPITALS stress a word.
- Designed voices are stored (1-year expiry, 200 per project). The description sets baseline delivery too: "thoughtful pauses" in it produced 1–1.8 s mid-line pauses that no per-line style removed.
- The model can change words. Seen in a 29-line narration: "Hmm, I get things wrong", "tell them" for "tell him". Anything with subtitles or a fixed script needs an ASR check (faster-whispermedium.en) and a retake.
- Cost: about 32 audio tokens per second of speech, $9/M through 2026-12-31 on 3.8 Flash TTS ($6/M Lite), so a minute is about $0.02.
- Voice replication (cloning from a 30 s sample plus a recorded consent clip) is not wired in, and is unavailable in the EEA, UK, Switzerland, India, Illinois and Texas.

## Basic Text Usage
import sys
sys.path.append('/mnt/skills/user/invoking-gemini/scripts')
from gemini_client import invoke_gemini

response = invoke_gemini(
    prompt="Explain quantum computing in 3 bullet points",
    model="flash",  # gemini-3.8-flash (default)
)
print(response)

## Structured Output

Use Pydantic models for guaranteed JSON Schema compliance:
from gemini_client import invoke_with_structured_output
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class BookAnalysis(BaseModel):
    title: str
    genre: str = Field(description="Primary genre")
    key_themes: list[str] = Field(max_length=5)
    rating: int = Field(ge=1, le=5)

result = invoke_with_structured_output(
    prompt="Analyze the book '1984' by George Orwell",
    pydantic_model=BookAnalysis
)
print(result.title)  # "1984"

Nested models are supported. Gemini'sresponseSchema rejects $ref/$defs,
which pydantic emits for every nested model, so the client inlines them before
sending:
class Finding(BaseModel):
    claim: str
    confidence: Literal["high", "medium", "low"]
    note: str | None = None

class Analysis(BaseModel):
    findings: list[Finding]     # nested — inlined for you
    gaps: list[str]

Budget output generously. Thinking tokens count againstmax_output_tokens
(default 32768). Too low and the JSON truncates mid-object, which surfaces as a
pydantic parse error rather than a length error — the client now detects
finishReason=MAX_TOKENS and says so explicitly.

## Parallel Invocation
from gemini_client import invoke_parallel

results = invoke_parallel(
    prompts=["Summarize Hamlet", "Summarize Macbeth", "Summarize Othello"],
    model="lite",  # gemini-3.5-flash-lite — cheap/fast tier for batch
)

## Available Models

The current frontier Flash is gemini-3.8-flash (GA 2026-09-02), the default and theflash alias. Google shipped three Flash generations in six
weeks: 3.6 (2026-07-21), 3.7 (2026-08-13), 3.8 (2026-09-02). Each stays
callable under a pinned alias (flash-3.7, flash-3.6, flash-3.5,
flash-3), and none has a shutdown date. gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview from
earlier docs is gone (shut down 2026-05-25).

The Pro tier is off routing.gemini-3.1-pro-preview costs 2.7× the input and
3.2× the output of 3.8 Flash at today's rates and loses to the 3.5+ Flash line
on the coding and agentic benchmarks that matter here. Do not target it; the
pro alias now resolves to gemini-3.8-flash, and "maximum reasoning" means
thinking_level='high' on Flash.

### Text / Reasoning Models

Model | Alias | Input/1M | Output/1M | Context | Notes 
---|---|---|---|---|---

绿涨红跌

涨跌幅与 K 线开盘时间

24 小时制

谷歌发布八项 AI 产品，包括 Gemini 4 Carbon 和 Hydrogen

关键要点

谷歌从周一到周四发布了八款 AI 产品，包括 Gemini 4 Carbon、Gemini 4 Hydrogen、TPU 8tx 和 TPU 8i Max 芯片。

Gemini 4 Carbon 的输入代币每百万个收费 2 美元，输出代币每百万个收费 10 美元，现已向付费开发者和谷歌 AI Ultra 订阅用户开放。

Gemini 4 Hydrogen 完成任务的速度是 Gemini 3.8 Flash 的 2.5 倍；Intelligent Eyewear 音频眼镜现已开放预订，提供三星和 Warby Parker 镜框。

谷歌 CEO Sundar Pichai 按天列出了谷歌本周一至周四发布的八款产品和研究项目。这些发布涵盖新款 TPU 芯片、Gemini 4 模型系列、DeepMind 研究工具、一款机器人模型、一个开发者决策端点以及智能眼镜。他帖文中的周五条目是 U2 的新专辑，Pichai 指出这并非谷歌的作品。

谷歌将 TPU 8tx 和 TPU 8i Max 加入第八代芯片系列

周一，谷歌推出 TPU 8tx 和 TPU 8i Max，使其第八代芯片系列今年增至四款系统。TPU 8tx 在数据处理过程中保持数据加密，面向政府机构和受监管企业。TPU 8i Max 将两颗 8i 芯片集成在同一个封装中，专为处理长上下文的 AI 智能体打造。

Gemini 4 Carbon 向付费开发者和企业开放

周二，谷歌顶级 Gemini 4 模型 Gemini 4 Carbon 向最初的一批安全测试人员之外的用户开放。付费开发者、企业和 Google AI Ultra 订阅用户现在都可以使用它。谷歌将这款模型定位为适用于长时间编码任务和网络防御。Carbon 的输入 token 价格为每百万个 2 美元，输出 token 价格为每百万个 10 美元。

DeepMind AlphaProof Code 验证 Signal 的加密代码

DeepMind 的 AlphaProof Code 使用由研究人员监督的 AI 智能体，为软件生成数学证明。它的首个目标是 Signal 背后的加密代码，团队称已在四周内完成验证。这些证明适用于一对一消息传递，而非整个应用；团队没有发现新的漏洞。

Gemini Robotics 2.5 改进工具操作能力及在人附近作业时的安全性

更新后的 Gemini Robotics 2.5 模型旨在帮助机器更准确地操作工具和柔软物体。DeepMind 表示，机器人完成任务的速度比早期版本快 20% 至 30%，并且在人附近时会表现得更加谨慎。Apptronik、Boston Dynamics 和 Agile Robots 是首批合作伙伴。

AlphaGenome 2 研究 DNA 变化对特定类型细胞的影响

AlphaGenome 2 研究 DNA 变化对特定类型细胞的影响，这可能有助于研究人员追踪疾病的起源。该模型基于超过 1.07 亿份细胞特征档案进行学习。学术人员可免费使用 API，企业可以加入私有预览，该模型尚未获准用于诊断。

Gemini Decisions API 返回是或否、选项选择和评分结果

开发者现在可以在 AI Studio 中使用 Gemini Decisions API 端点，该端点专为快速判定而设计。它会返回是或否、从给定选项中选出一项，或给出一个分数，不会提供文字答复。其背后的 Gemini Decision 1 模型输入 token 价格为每百万个 0.10 美元，输出免费，并提供免费层级。

Gemini 4 Hydrogen 发布，成为速度更快、成本更低的 Gemini 4 模型

周四，Gemini 4 Hydrogen 发布，成为 Gemini 4 系列中速度更快、成本更低的成员。Pichai 表示，它完成任务的速度比 Gemini 3.8 Flash 快 2.5 倍，并允许用户从四种推理深度中进行选择。用户可以在 Gemini 应用、Search、AI Studio 和 Gemini API 中使用它。

Intelligent Eyewear 音频眼镜开放预订

周四，首款 Android XR 音频眼镜也开始接受预订，产品以 Intelligent Eyewear 名义销售。谷歌与 Samsung 合作打造这款眼镜，镜框由 Warby Parker 和 Gentle Monster 设计。眼镜可将 Gemini 的声音传入佩戴者耳中，并支持 Android 和 iPhone。文章称，这款眼镜预计将在假日季期间发货。

谷歌本周八项 AI 发布的关键信息

周一：TPU 8tx 和 TPU 8i Max 使谷歌第八代芯片系列今年增至四款系统。

TPU 8tx 在数据处理过程中保持数据加密，面向政府机构和受监管企业。

# Google unveils Gemini 4, new TPUs, smart glasses in five-day AI blitz

Google CEO Sundar Pichai announced eight major AI and hardware releases over five days, including new TPU systems and Gemini 4 models. These updates target developers, businesses, and AI researchers with enhanced capabilities.

## Highlights

- Google CEO Sundar Pichai detailed eight major AI and hardware releases in five days.
- New TPU 8tx and 8i Max systems enhance encrypted processing and AI agent capabilities.
- Gemini 4 Carbon is now available for developers, businesses, and AI Ultra subscribers.
- Android XR audio glasses pre-orders started, developed with Samsung and Warby Parker.

Google CEO Sundar Pichai outlined eight major product and research project releases over five days, from Monday to Thursday. The announcements included two new TPU systems, two Gemini 4 models, three DeepMind projects, a developer API, and pre-orders for Android XR audio glasses.

### Key AI and Hardware Updates
Two new TPU systems, TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, were introduced on Monday, expanding Google's eighth-generation chip family to four systems. The 8tx system is designed for encrypted data processing, targeting governments and regulated firms. The 8i Max combines two 8i chips for AI agents handling extensive contexts.
Gemini 4 Carbon, Google's advanced Gemini 4 model, became available to paying developers, businesses, and Google AI Ultra subscribers on Tuesday. It is positioned for complex coding tasks and cyber defence, costing $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.DeepMind's AlphaProof Code project employs AI agents to generate mathematical proofs for software, verifying Signal's encryption code in four weeks. This verification applied to one-to-one messaging within the app and found no new flaws.

Gemini Robotics 2.5 was updated to improve how machines handle tools and soft objects, with DeepMind reporting a 20 per cent to 30 per cent quicker job completion rate. Partners include Apptronik, Boston Dynamics, and Agile Robots.

AlphaGenome 2, a science release on Wednesday, investigates how DNA changes affect specific cell types. This research could aid in tracing disease origins. Academics can access its API for free, while companies can join a private preview. It is not approved for diagnosis.

The Gemini Decisions API, also released on Wednesday, offers an AI Studio endpoint for rapid verdicts. It provides yes/no responses, selections from options, or scores, without written output. The underlying Gemini Decision 1 model costs $0.10 per million input tokens, with free output and a free tier.Gemini 4 Hydrogen, launched on Thursday, is a faster and more cost-effective Gemini 4 model. Pichai noted it completes tasks 2.5 times quicker than Gemini 3.8 Flash and offers four reasoning depths. It is accessible via the Gemini app, Search, AI Studio, and the Gemini API.

Pre-orders for the first Android XR audio glasses, branded as Intelligent Eyewear, began on Thursday. Developed with Samsung and featuring frames by Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, these glasses integrate Gemini into the wearer's ear and support Android and iPhone. Shipments are expected during the holiday season.

## Llama 3.3 70B API

Llama 3.3 70B is a large language model by Meta, available on the Venice API asllama-3.3-70b. It runs privately, with zero data retention.

Llama 3.3 70B is Meta's instruction-tuned 70-billion-parameter Llama model, which Meta reports performs close to its much larger Llama 3.1 405B on many tasks. It supports text input and output with a 128K-token context window, for chat, writing and code.

M

# Meta

脸书

### 企业简介

Meta Platforms, Inc. 是美国上市科技公司，收入以广告为主，2021 年 10 月由 Facebook, Inc. 更名而来；人工智能为另一核心方向，覆盖 Llama、Muse 模型与 Meta AI 助手、AI 眼镜。Facebook 等应用是旗下产品品牌，非公司主体。s-AI↔DeepTHink.cn

## 一、基本信息

名称与主体口径是阅读这家公司的第一道门槛：母公司、产品品牌与硬件品牌分属不同层级，四项名称分别取自交易所披露、官方文件与官网中文页面。官方简体与繁体中文页面只使用「Meta」这一品牌名，未登记中文法定公司名；中文资料里的「脸书／脸谱」指的是 Facebook 产品，不是公司主体。下表按登记与披露口径汇总主体身份，并列出各字段的日期口径。

项目 | 内容 
---|---
常用品牌或别名 | Meta（母体品牌，官网中英文版通用）；Facebook、Instagram、WhatsApp、Messenger、Threads 为旗下产品；Meta Quest、Ray-Ban Meta、Oakley Meta 为硬件产品；中文资料常见的「脸书／脸谱」指 Facebook 产品，非公司主体名 
名称说明 | 官方简体中文、繁体中文页面及官方中文新闻稿均只用「Meta」品牌名，未登记中文法定公司名称；未见两个独立权威来源使用同一中文译名，故中文全称留白，中文简称取官网品牌名。「Meta」在中文语境既指品牌也指上市主体 
曾用名 | TheFacebook, Inc.（2004 年注册）、Facebook, Inc.（2005-09-20 至 2021-10-28）；更名与注册沿革见纽约市与加州总检察长诉讼文件 
机构类型 | 企业（美国特拉华州注册的上市公司） 
成立时间 | 官方人物页称 2004 年以 Facebook 之名创立；政府诉讼文件记载 2004-07-29 在特拉华州注册为 TheFacebook, Inc.，两者口径并列 
创始人或创始团队 | Mark Zuckerberg（马克·扎克伯格，官方人物页与政府诉讼文件确认）；官网与官方文件未列其他共同创立者名单 
总部所在地 | 美国加利福尼亚州门洛帕克（Menlo Park, California），政府诉讼文件记为「principal place of business」，官方财报署名地同为门洛帕克 
注册地 | 美国特拉华州（政府诉讼文件、SEC 披露） 
现任核心负责人 | Mark Zuckerberg（创始人、董事长兼首席执行官，截至 2026-10-21 官方财报）；Susan Li（李苏珊，首席财务官，据财联社 2026-10-22 电话会报道）；Dina Powell McCormick（总裁兼副董事长，据 CNBC 2026-11-11 报道） 
员工规模 | 66,775 人（截至 2026-09-30，官方 2026 年第三季度财报），同比减少 15% 
上市状态 | 已上市（NASDAQ：META，Class A 普通股） 
官方网站 | https://www.meta.com/ 

注册地与实际总部分离是最容易混淆的一项口径：前者决定法律披露归属，门洛帕克则是日常经营与决策所在地，两者分别对应政府文件与财报署名地。

## 二、公司背景

公司的前身是 2004 年上线的校园社交网站，此后扩展为覆盖数十亿用户的多产品平台，2012 年上市、2021 年更名。s-AI↔DeepTHink.cn更名只调整母公司名称，各款应用保持原有品牌、公司结构亦未改变；母公司、产品品牌与主体财务分属不同层级，主体层面的登记沿革与股权安排因此成为理解这家公司的关键。

### 1. 创立背景

官方人物页写明扎克伯格于 2004 年以 Facebook 为公司名称创立本公司，2021 年 10 月更名为 Meta，以反映旗下应用家族的全部产品与服务，并专注开发元宇宙社群体验。纽约市与加州总检察长提交的诉讼文件则记载，公司于 2004-07-29 在特拉华州注册为 TheFacebook, Inc.，2005-09-20 改名 Facebook, Inc.，2021-10-28 改为现名。官网给出的是创立年份，政府文件给出的是具体注册日，两者相差数月。

### 2. 股权与关联关系

上市主体为 Meta Platforms, Inc.，Class A 普通股在纳斯达克交易、一股一票；Class B 为未单独公开交易的高投票权股份，每股 10 票，可按一比一转换为 A 类。SEC 备案文件记载，扎克伯格持有接近全部流通的 Class B 股份，约对应 61% 的总体投票权与约 14% 的经济权益；雅虎财经 2026 年报道给出约 60.6% 投票权、约 13.4% 股权，两者差异来自时点与计算口径。2026-10-21 财报宣布，董事会批准设立无投票权 Class C 普通股，拟于 2027-01-19 生效，并以每股派发一股 C 类的方式形成等效一拆二的股票股息；公司说明该股息不改变任何股东的投票权。

### 3. 核心团队

官方财报与人物页确认扎克伯格为创始人、董事长兼首席执行官。s-AI↔DeepTHink.cn财联社对 2026 年第三季度电话会的报道列出 Susan Li 为首席财务官；CNBC 2026-11-11 报道列出 Dina Powell McCormick 为总裁兼副董事长，并说明由她与技术负责人 Daniel Gross 领衔 Meta Compute 算力基础设施计划；该计划负责数据中心与相关基础设施的建设运营。

## 三、主营业务

公司自 2021 年第四季度起按两大分部披露财务：应用家族（Family of Apps，FoA）与 Reality Labs（RL）。前者承载 Facebook、Instagram、Messenger、WhatsApp 等社交、通讯与内容产品，收入几乎全部来自广告；后者覆盖虚拟现实与增强现实相关的消费硬件、软件与内容，包括 Meta Quest 头显与 AI 眼镜。官方财报按此口径分别列示收入与经营损益，广告收入计入应用家族，分部数据与合并报表数据不可混用。两大分部的规模差异明显：应用家族承担流量与变现，Reality Labs 仍处投入期，当季经营亏损持续。

广告变现依赖展示量与单价两个变量，公司把人工智能投入列为提升互动、推荐与变现效率的路径。2026 年第三季度财报中，管理层称 AI 投资已通过更强的用户互动、更好的推荐与更高效的变现带来增量广告收入；同期官方披露广告展示量同比增长 10%、平均广告价格同比增长 14%。应用家族其他收入则主要来自 WhatsApp 付费消息与订阅业务。

## 四、主要产品与服务

产品按两大分部归类：应用家族提供社交、通讯、内容与 AI 助手，Reality Labs 提供头显与 AI 眼镜，模型与开发者服务单列。s-AI↔DeepTHink.cn下表按分部列出主要产品，当前状态以官方财报、官方产品页与官方开发者文档的时点为准。

产品谱系显示，社交与通讯应用承担流量与广告变现，AI 眼镜与头显归属仍处投入期的 Reality Labs；模型层则同时保留开放权重的 Llama 与闭源的 Muse 两条线。

## 五、AI 业务与优势

公司把「个人超级智能」（personal superintelligence）列为官方愿景，AI 工作覆盖开放权重的 Llama 系列、闭源前沿模型 Muse 系列、跨应用的 Meta AI 助手与 Muse 智能体、AI 眼镜等可穿戴，以及支撑推荐、广告与模型训练的自建算力。模型能力、许可证条款与基准成绩以官方研究博客、模型卡、开发者文档与开源仓库为准，第三方评测另作参照。

### 1. AI 布局与时间线

官方 AI 站点把个人超级智能列为愿景，并列出研究项目 SAM 3、DINOv3、V-JEPA 2、Brain2Qwerty 与自研 MTIA 芯片。官方研究博客称公司在约十四个月前对 AI 工作进行了彻底重组，重组后的 Meta Superintelligence Labs（超级智能实验室，MSL）先后推出 Muse Spark 与 Muse Wonder 系列。主要发布节点集中在 2025 年 4 月至 2026 年 10 月：

- 2025-04-05：Llama 4 社区许可证生效，Scout 与 Maverick 提供开放权重下载。
- 2026-04-08：MSL 首个模型 Muse Spark 发布，官方站点同期刊出「Scaling Towards Personal Superintelligence」等三篇说明。
- 2026-06-23：官方宣布与 EssilorLuxottica 合作推出 Meta Glasses。
- 2026-07-07、2026-07-09：Muse Image、Muse Video 与 Muse Spark 1.1 相继发布；Meta Model API 进入公开预览。
- 2026-10-12：Muse Wonder 与 Muse Wonder Full 上线，官方开发者博客同日公布接口定价。

### 2. 代表模型与产品

据官方 Llama 页，Llama 4 采用原生多模态与混合专家架构，列出 Maverick 与 Scout 两款，二者均给出 1000 万 token 级上下文，Scout 标注可在单张 H100 GPU 上运行；同页列出 Llama 3.1、3.2、3.3 等既有版本。Muse 一侧，官方新闻稿称 Muse Wonder 与 Muse Wonder Full 面向个人与专业智能体任务，具备 Active Memory 与 Active Focus，强调法律、金融、健康等专门领域与长时编码能力；官方开发者文档给出 100 万 token 推理上下文，模型卡列出文本、图像、视频与音频输入。开发者通过 Meta Model API 与 Muse Code 调用，官方开发者博客公布的价格为每百万输入 token 4 美元、每百万输出 token 20 美元（USD），Muse Wonder Full 仅限 Muse Code 订阅方案。消费侧有 Meta AI 助手与独立应用、Vibes 创作体验，硬件侧有与 EssilorLuxottica 合作的 AI 眼镜产品线。

### 3. 优势与依据s-AI↔DeepTHink.cn

证据强度可分为三层：官方许可证全文与模型卡属一手依据，官方博客的基准成绩属公司自报，第三方核对另作参照。

- 许可证全文：Llama 4 Community License Agreement（2025-04-05 生效）授予非独占、全球、不可转让、免版税的有限许可，允许使用、复制、分发、创建衍生作品与修改；分发时须随附协议、显著标注「Built with Llama」、衍生模型名称以「Llama」开头并保留 Notice 归属声明，且须遵守可接受使用政策。官方开发者页与 Hugging Face 模型卡均载有全文。
- 同一许可证第 2 条规定，若被许可方在 Llama 4 版本发布日前一个月的月活跃用户超过 7 亿，须另行向 Meta 申请授权；第 5 条规定起诉 Meta 侵权即终止许可；第 7 条规定适用加州法律、由加州法院专属管辖。
- 官方 Llama 页列出的基准成绩为 Meta 自报，测试条件为零样本、temperature=0、不使用多数投票或并行测试时计算，高方差基准取多次生成平均；该页 MMLU Pro 一栏 Maverick 为 80.5、Scout 为 74.3。
- 官方研究博客称 Muse Wonder 系列在个人与专业智能体、记忆与编码基准上取得同类最佳结果，并称训练于千兆瓦级的 Prometheus 数据中心，属公司自报；第三方技术媒体核对后指出，官方对比表 14 行中有 7 行由竞品得分更高。
- 2026 年第三季度财报称 AI 投资已带来增量广告收入，并给出全年资本开支 1,350 亿至 1,450 亿美元（USD）的指引；官方 Connect 2026 博客列出 AI 眼镜与 Muse 语音、实时 avatar 等整合方向。

### 4. 局限与不确定性

Llama 4 社区许可证含月活阈值、命名约束与诉讼终止条款，并非开放源代码促进会意义上的通用开源许可证；官方自报的基准成绩尚未附完整独立复现报告，训练与评测条件由公司单方给出。新一代主力模型已转向闭源 Muse 系列，Llama 后续更新节奏未见官方确认。财务侧，2026 年第三季度自由现金流为负 21.2 亿美元，Reality Labs 当季经营亏损 41.29 亿美元，AI 投入的回报周期由财报自行提示长于核心业务。

### 2. 估值与资本动向

DeepSeek.content:
# Use DeepSeek with the AI Gateway

Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/providers/deepseek

Call DeepSeek models through the ngrok AI Gateway with ngrok.ai credits or your own DeepSeek API key, and check its peak and off-peak pricing.

DeepSeek provides high-performance reasoning and chat models.

DeepSeek supports Chat Completions, Responses, and Anthropic Messages requests.

[!NOTE]

DeepSeek is a built-in provider you can pay for with credits, so a provider key is optional.
Add your own DeepSeek key to bill usage to your DeepSeek account instead of your ngrok.ai credits.

## Setup

### 1. Create an access key and add credits

Follow the quickstart to create an access key and purchase credits in app.ngrok.ai.

### 2. Store your DeepSeek API key (optional)

Skip this step to pay with credits. To bring your own key, sign up at platform.deepseek.com and create an API key. Then add a provider key and create an access key configuration with adeepseek routing rule that uses it.

### 3. Send requests

Send requests with your access key:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1",
    api_key="ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="deepseek-flash",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)

## Peak and off-peak pricing

DeepSeek charges double its off-peak price during peak hours: 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday, except Chinese public holidays. All other hours are off-peak.

- Pay with credits: ngrok.ai charges DeepSeek's off-peak price at every hour, including peak hours.
- Your own DeepSeek key: DeepSeek bills you directly, at its peak price during peak hours.

See DeepSeek's pricing page for current prices.

## Available models

See the model catalog.deepseek-flash is DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.
DeepSeek has retired V4 Flash and serves requests for deepseek-v4-flash with V4.1 Flash, so use deepseek-flash in new code.

DeepSeek.content:
# 突发！DeepSeek开放全家桶API：官方App功能均可自由组合调用

##### 一水 发自 凹非寺
量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI

周五晚上搞事，D老师通通都不藏了！

就在刚刚，DeepSeek宣布，正式开放全家桶应用API。

什么意思？

以前大家在DeepSeek App里用得顺手的联网搜索、深度思考搜索、文件上传、链接阅读等功能，现在开发者通过API通通都能直接用上了，而且不必打包使用，它们都有独立接口，支持单独调用、分别计费。

划重点，语音能力也首次加入开放行列，包括语音识别、语音合成等接口。

官方还放出一句相当有意思的话：

开发者甚至可以1:1复刻出完整的DeepSeek App。

不是哥们，连自家产品都允许别人照着做啊？？

DeepSeek还贴心亲自打了个样，直接开源了一套轻量级聊天前端Demo，支持导入DeepSeek历史对话。

也就是说，开发者不用再从头折腾搜索、文件解析、语音识别这些基础功能，就能快速搭出一个功能接近DeepSeek App的产品。

消息一出，评论区也是相当热闹。

有网友直接感叹：

什么叫1:1复刻出完整的DeepSeek App？？？人工智能之光！

## 全家桶应用API开放一览

具体来看，这次DeepSeek一口气开放了这些能力：

这里有两个变化值得单独说说。

首先，联网搜索其实不是第一次开放，早在今年10月17日，DeepSeek就已经开放了自研Search和Fetch接口。

但当时，开发者还需要自己处理不少工具调用和模型之间的衔接工作。

比如用户问“最近AI圈发生了什么”，开发者需要先让模型判断要不要搜索，再调用Search找网页、用Fetch读取内容，最后把结果重新交给模型总结。

这一整套流程，都得开发者自己写代码串起来。

现在就简单多了。

开发者只要给模型打开联网搜索功能，什么时候搜索、搜什么、要读哪些网页，以及如何根据搜索结果继续回答，DeepSeek都会自动完成。

其次是语音，这次终于有了官方独立接口。

此前，DeepSeek App虽然已经支持语音交互，但公开的模型API并没有提供同样完整的语音能力。

开发者想做一个能听会说的DeepSeek助手，通常还需要另外接入语音识别、语音合成服务。

现在，ASR和TTS都可以通过DeepSeek官方接口调用了。

而且，上述底层能力也不必全部打包使用。

DeepSeek还提供了Search、Fetch、OCR、ASR、TTS等独立接口，开发者可以按需选择、自由组合。

目前，V4.1-Flash模型已在Messages、Responses和Chat Completions三类接口下支持相关对话扩展功能。

换句话说，D老师这次是把自家App背后的整套基础能力，像积木一样全部交到了开发者手里。

那么问题来了：

功能给得这么全，价格又如何？

## 语音识别一小时不到4毛，DeepSeek这次还打五折

先看DeepSeek这次公布的工具API价格表：

最扎眼的，当然是语音。

语音识别原价0.78元/小时，目前直接打五折，只要0.39元。

换算下来，一分钟大约0.0065元，识别一小时录音，连4毛钱都不到。

语音合成同样五折，原价每万字符3元，现在只要1.5元。

什么概念？

对比一下国外主流厂商的语音API价格：

OpenAI的GPT-Transcribe，识别一小时音频需要0.27美元（约合人民币1.81元）。

即便是更便宜的GPT-4o mini Transcribe，也要0.18美元（约合人民币1.21元）。

Google Cloud的标准语音识别服务，按0.016美元/分钟计算，一小时是0.96美元（约合人民币6.43元）。

相比之下，DeepSeek目前的0.39元，分别只有上述三款服务价格的约1/4.6、1/3.1和1/16.5。

至于搜索和网页抓取，依旧是此前公布的每1000次成功调用5元。

文字识别OCR则为每1000页1.5元，平均识别一页只要0.0015元。

这么一看，DeepSeek这次的定价思路也挺清楚。

原有的搜索能力保持低价，新开放的语音接口再用五折优惠降低使用门槛。

对于想做语音助手、会议记录、文档处理等应用的开发者来说，至少基础工具的调用成本，已经被压到了相当低的水平。

（D老师还是你D老师）

## One More Thing

最后，还有个挺有意思的细节。

DeepSeek在公告末尾写道：

DeepSeek现有的对话产品只是较为基础的一种形态。

这话倒也符合D老师一贯以来的画风。

一直以来，相比花大力气经营C端产品，DeepSeek似乎更愿意把精力放在模型研发上。

DeepSeek App虽已积累了大量C端用户，但从产品形态上看，依然是大家熟悉的聊天助手。

如今，它干脆把所有能力全部开放，甚至连复刻自家APP的示例代码都准备好，颇有一种：

模型我继续研究，应用该怎么玩，就交给大家来摸索的意思。

怎么说呢？这招还挺机智的。。。

回头看移动互联网时代，微信、抖音这些超级应用，几乎重塑了人们社交、娱乐乃至获取信息的方式。

而到了AI时代，大模型已经越来越强，应用形态却似乎还没跟上。

从ChatGPT到DeepSeek，大家最熟悉的交互方式，依然是打开一个聊天框，输入问题，等待回答。

但AI的下一款超级应用，真的还会是一个聊天框吗？

眼下谁也没有答案。

既然如此，与其自己关起门来猜，不如把工具都摆出来，让全世界的开发者一起试。

万一真有人折腾出了下一个爆款呢？

真就D老师大舞台，有脑洞你就来。（doge）

一键三连「点赞」「转发」「小心心」

欢迎在评论区留下你的想法！

DeepSeek.content:
# DeepSeek开放全家桶API：以后可以随心所欲构建APP了

摘要：DeepSeek正式开放全家桶应用 API：在原有API中开启对应参数，即可获得深度思考搜索、文件输入等对话功能；语音及相关底层能力也已开放独立接口。开发者可以在自己的应用中轻松实现复杂的对话功能，甚至1:1复刻出完整的DeepSeek App。

在 DeepSeek App（含网页端）的对话服务中，联网搜索、文件输入、阅读链接、语音交互及安全等能力与模型推理相互配合，构成了用户熟悉的对话体验。而开发者如果想要在应用中实现类似功能，除接入原有 DeepSeek API 外，往往还需耗费大量精力去对接外部工具、处理调用衔接。

今天，我们正式开放这套全家桶应用 API：在原有 API 中开启对应参数，即可获得深度思考搜索、文件输入等对话功能；语音及相关底层能力也已开放独立接口（含 OCR、ASR、TTS 等），支持单独或组合调用。开发者可以在自己的应用中轻松实现复杂的对话功能，甚至 1:1 复刻出完整的 DeepSeek App。

全面开放应用功能，支持独立调用

本次更新将 DeepSeek App 的各项交互功能直接整合进原有 API。开启对应参数后，相关工具调用与上下文拼接均由服务端自动完成。目前，V4.1-Flash 模型（deepseek-flash）已在 Messages、Responses 与 Chat Completions 接口下支持以下能力：

联网搜索：在非思考模式下，打开 deepseek_web_search 工具后，模型可根据提问自动发起网页或图片搜索并附引用作答；

深度思考搜索：在思考模式下，打开 deepseek_web_search 工具后，模型可在多步推理中自主联网搜索与阅读链接；

文件输入：支持上传 PDF、Office、图片等格式的文件，完成纯文本提取或图文混排解析后，拼入对话上下文供模型作答；

阅读链接：将 deepseek_read_url 工具打开后，模型可自动识别用户消息中的链接，抓取网页内容并结合上下文作答；

模型安全：开启安全校验参数后，我们将提供基础风控，审核模型输入输出，命中风险时返回拒答标识。如您对外提供应用服务，请务必开启该参数，并承担内容安全审核、大模型登记、AI 标识等义务。

此外，为方便开发者更灵活地接入自有工作流，上述底层能力及语音能力均支持作为独立接口单独调用，包括：Search、Fetch、OCR、ASR、TTS。

使用上述接口，开发者即可实现与 DeepSeek App 基本一致的功能。为直观演示这一效果，我们基于新版 API 构建并开源了一份轻量的前端 Demo，支持直接导入 DeepSeek 历史对话。

Demo 体验入口：https://cdn.deepseek.com/chat-demo

示例代码入口：https://github.com/deepseek-ai/chat-demo

更详细的参数定义与调用说明，请参考 DeepSeek 官方 API 文档 [API 指南 - 构建 Chatbot]。

API 定价说明

用户调用 DeepSeek API 使用扩展能力时，除收取 Token 费用外，也将收取相关工具的调用费用。各项工具价格如下表所示：

我们相信，人与模型的交互依然充满无限可能，而 DeepSeek 现有的对话产品只是较为基础的一种形态。

现在，官方产品背后的各项能力均已支持通过 DeepSeek API 随心调用、自由组合，我们期待开发者能够借此省去重复的基础工作，打造出更多样、更极致、更具想象力的产品。

欢迎使用 DeepSeek API，尽情创造。

DAMO开发者矩阵 DeepSeek 开放全家桶 API、Edge0 145B 进笔记本、联想建词元工厂｜AI 新闻日报 11-15

# DeepSeek 开放全家桶 API、Edge0 145B 进笔记本、联想建词元工厂｜AI 新闻日报 11-15

主题： DeepSeek 把 App 的搜索、文件、语音能力整体开放成接口；Edge0 放出 145B 开放权重模型，笔记本 29GB 内存可跑；Thinking Machines 补放 594B 的 Inkling 2 Small 权重；Perplexity 开源决策模型 Decider 1.3 并加入片段定位；具身侧曦选创智 5 亿元天使轮、优理奇 5 亿元 Pre-A、思灵 5 亿美元 F 轮、妙动 Beni 国内首发

编制时间： 2026 年 11 月 15 日 07:00（北京时间）

本期看点： 模型公司开始把产品能力当作 API 商品拆开卖，DeepSeek 一次放出五项对话能力与五个独立接口，工具调用与上下文拼接改由服务端完成；本地推理的硬件门槛继续下探，145B 稀疏 MoE 在 48GB 笔记本上的峰值内存报到 29GB，代价是自定义许可证禁止独立商业编码助手；开源与开放权重再次被区分，594B 的 Apache 标签下另有一份可接受使用政策；决策模型这条支线出现开源版本，分类与抽取不再需要逐 token 生成；具身侧一周内四笔融资，芯片定义权成为合资的核心动因。

### 一、要闻速览

序号 | 方向 | 事件 | 关键数字 
---|---|---|---
1 | AI Coding | DeepSeek 开放全家桶应用 API | 5 项对话能力；5 个独立接口；搜索与抓取 5 元/千次 
2 | AI Coding | Edge0 放出 145B 与 120B 开放权重 | 145B 总参、10.12B 激活；29GB 峰值；80+ token/s 
3 | AI Coding | Thinking Machines 补放 Inkling 2 Small 权重 | 594B 总参、17B 激活；NVFP4 需 500GB 显存 
4 | AI Coding | Perplexity 开源 Decider 1.3 与 Flash | 27B 与 4B；63 项分类 91.6%；每百万输入 0.02 美元 
5 | 具身智能 | 曦选创智 5 亿元天使轮，投后 40 亿元 | 沐曦与优必选各持 35.01%；2027H2 流片、2028 量产 
6 | 具身智能 | 优理奇 UniX AI 完成 5 亿元 Pre-A | 月出货超百台、峰值 300 台；单机连续出杯 2156 杯 
7 | 具身智能 | 思灵机器人 5 亿美元 F 轮 | 投后估值 85 亿美元；累计融资 20 亿美元 
8 | 具身智能 | 妙动 Beni 多地形跟拍机器人国内首发 | 众筹超 500 万美元、7926 名支持者；标准套装 4999 元 

### 二、AI Coding 深度动态

#### 1. DeepSeek 把 App 的对话能力整体开放成接口

事件。 11 月 13 日，DeepSeek 在 API 变更日志中发布「全家桶应用 API」，把 DeepSeek App（含网页端）里与模型推理配合的那套交互能力，直接并入原有 API。开发者开启对应参数即可获得联网搜索、深度思考搜索、文件输入、阅读链接与模型安全校验，工具调用与上下文拼接由服务端完成。

核心参数与产品细节。

- 接口覆盖：在 Messages、Responses 与 Chat Completions 三套协议下，模型 deepseek-flash（当前服务 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017）支持上述五项能力，其中联网搜索需关闭思考模式并开启 deepseek_web_search 工具，深度思考搜索则在思考模式下启用同一工具，由模型在多步推理中自主检索并阅读链接。
- 文件与链接：文件输入支持 PDF、Office 文档与图片，经纯文本提取或图文混排解析后拼入上下文；阅读链接由 deepseek_read_url 工具识别消息中的 URL，抓取页面后结合上下文作答。
- 独立接口：底层能力与语音能力均可单独调用，包含 Search、Fetch、OCR、ASR、TTS，可组合进自有工作流。
- 计费口径：搜索与网页抓取每千次 5 元（海外站 0.75 美元），文件解析与 OCR 每千页 0.225 美元，语音合成每万字符 0.45 美元、语音识别每小时 0.116 美元，语音两项当前为半价；搜索与抓取费用在直接调用与该工具被模型自行调用两种情况下都收取。
- token 价格：deepseek-flash 维持每百万输入 0.30 美元（缓存未命中）、输出 1.20 美元，错峰时段减半。
- 配套物料：官方开源 chat-demo，一个静态网页客户端，浏览器直连 API，支持深度思考、搜索、链接阅读、附件与语音输入，并可导入用户的历史对话；另发布《Build a Chatbot》接入文档。
- 合规提示：对外提供应用服务需开启安全校验参数，并承担内容安全审核、大模型登记与 AI 标识等义务。

值得关注的原因。 这次开放的价值不在模型能力，在于把「产品形态」变成可采购的部件。过去要复刻一个对话助手，开发者需要自己接搜索引擎、自己做文档解析、自己维护多轮上下文，任何一环出问题都要自己排查；现在这些环节收到服务端，接口只是开关。对中小团队来说，交付方式从搭系统变成配参数，周期会明显缩短。另一面也要看清，工具调用被托管之后，检索质量、抓取成功率、拒答策略都由平台决定，可调试的空间变小；官方在文档中强调的登记与标识义务，实际上是把这部分合规责任转移给了调用方。

# Change Log
## Date: 2026-11-13
### Releasing the full suite of application APIs
In the DeepSeek App (including the web version), web search, file input, URL reading, voice interaction and safety work together with model inference to form the conversation experience users know. Today we open these capabilities to developers: enable the corresponding parameters in the existing APIs to get conversation features such as web search, file input and URL reading, with the tool calls and context assembly handled by the service.
The `deepseek-flash` model supports the following in the Messages, Responses and Chat Completions APIs:
- **Web search**: with thinking disabled and the `deepseek_web_search` tool enabled, the model runs web or image searches as the question requires and answers with citations.
- **Deep thinking search**: with thinking enabled and the `deepseek_web_search` tool enabled, the model searches the web and reads links on its own over multiple reasoning steps.
- **File input**: upload PDFs, Office files, images, and more; after plain-text extraction or rich-layout parsing, they are added to the conversation context for the model to answer from.
- **URL reading**: with the `deepseek_read_url` tool enabled, the model detects links in the user message, fetches the pages and answers with them in context.
- **Model safety**: with the safety check parameter enabled, we provide basic risk control: the model input and output are reviewed, and a refusal marker is returned when a risk is found. If you provide a service to the public, enable this parameter and fulfill obligations such as content safety review, large model registration and AI labeling.

**ON THIS PAGE**

#### 2. Edge0 放出 145B 权重，笔记本跑得动，许可证写着限制

事件。 11 月 11 日，Edge0 在 Hugging Face 上传 Edge0-145B 与 Edge0-120B 两组权重，同时放出统一推理框架与部署工具，次日发布技术博客。公司口径是「首个能在个人电脑上运行的开源 145B 模型」，11 月 14 日该发布在 Hacker News 首页拿到 334 分。

核心参数与产品细节。

- 架构：潜在稀疏 MoE，145B 总参数、每 token 约 10.12B 激活，48 层，每层 512 个专家，路由 10 个加 1 个共享专家，上下文 128K 至 256K，训练原生采用 4bit 格式。
- 权重体积：Q3_K 版 40.81 GiB、NVFP4 版 47.79 GiB；四个仓库合计 90 至 113 GB，下载并非 29GB。
- 笔记本数据：厂商标称 48GB 内存笔记本上峰值内存约 29GB、预填 1100+ token/s、解码 80+ token/s、整机功耗约 120W，128K 至 256K 上下文下速度基本不变。
- 单卡数据：模型卡给出 RTX 5090 上 Q3_K 解码 121.2 token/s、16K 预填 3554.9 token/s；NVFP4 解码 98.3 token/s。
- 内存分层：每组 64 个专家共享两个大矩阵，热专家驻显存，约 40GB 专家库放系统内存，约 48GB 词表数据留在 SSD 按需读取，CPU 与 GPU 分担计算并叠加投机解码。
- 许可证：自定义的 edge0-community-model-1.0，允许个人与研究使用、允许修改与商业使用输出，但模型销售、付费推理服务、独立的商业编码或办公助手需单独书面许可，同时受上游 Qwen 社区许可约束。
- 基准：全部为厂商自测，Terminal-Bench 2.1 为 86.52、GPQA-Diamond 90.4、DeepSWE 1.1 为 64.6，六项均值 72.8，技术报告尚未发布。

值得关注的原因。 这条的关键词是「开放权重」而不是「开源」。按 OSI 定义，可自由销售与提供推理服务是必要条件，edge0-community-model-1.0 恰恰在这两处设了闸门，而公告与多家转述都用了 open-source 的说法，读者需要按许可证原文判断能否商用。技术侧的看点则是内存分层：把专家库放内存、词表放 SSD，用带宽换容量，这套思路在 MoE 时代的消费级硬件上有普适性。真正的验证点在第三方复现，尤其是长上下文下的解码速度与 29GB 这个数字的测量口径，博客里对笔记本型号只写了「兼容的个人笔记本」。

#### 3. Thinking Machines 补放 594B 权重，Apache 标签下另有条款

事件。 11 月 5 日，Thinking Machines Lab 发布 594B 参数的 Inkling 2 Small，当时为闭权重，公告称权重将在完成进一步安全评估后开放。11 月 12 日，公告页更新确认权重已上架 Hugging Face，仓库不打门禁，许可证标签为 Apache 2.0。

核心参数与产品细节。

- 架构：48 层混合专家 Transformer，594B 总参数、每 token 17B 激活，每个 token 路由到 384 个专家中的 8 个，接受文本与图像输入、输出文本，上下文 1M，原生 NVFP4 训练。
- 显存底线：模型卡列出两个检查点，NVFP4 需 500GB 聚合显存（2 张 B300 或 4 张 H200），MXFP8 需 800GB（4 张 B300 或 8 张 H200）；卡片称 MXFP8 在评测上只高 1 至 2 个百分点，建议使用 NVFP4。
- 评测数字：SWE-bench Pro v2 的 Hard 子集 86.3%、BrowseComp 90.2%（带 compaction）、ARC-AGI-2 81.7%、HLE-Diamond 28.7%，Terminal Bench Science v0.1 仅 5.7%；多数第三方分数引自榜单所有者自己的报告。
- 训练：预训练 8.4 万亿 token，联合强化学习在 2048 张 GPU 上跑 9 天。
- 下载情况：截至 11 月 14 日，仓库 3,647 次下载、304 个赞。
- 官方自述短板：聊天场景打磨不足，对安全相关提问有时反应过度，在技能较多的代码库里容易选错工具，对齐结果落后于 GPT-6.1 Sol 一类闭源模型。
- 口径出入：公告称自动化研究案例中预测分数「翻了一倍多」，附表是从 0.191 到 0.289，约 50%。

值得关注的原因。 594B 的体量与 1M 上下文放在开放权重阵营里属于第一梯队，但 500GB 的显存底线决定了它落地在机架而不是工作站，这与同周 Edge0 的路线正好相反：一个用内存分层换单机可用，一个用参数规模换能力上限。许可证层面还留了一个坑，仓库标 Apache 2.0，而公告同时链接了一份可接受使用政策，标签并不描述政策条款，企业采购时需要两份文件一起看。性能方面，Terminal Bench Science 的 5.7% 说明它在需要严谨实验设计的任务上明显偏弱，选型时不宜按单一榜单推断。

#### 4. Perplexity 开源 Decider 1.3，分类与抽取不再逐 token 生成

事件。 11 月 12 日，Perplexity 在开发者论坛发布 Decider v1.3 与 Decider Flash v1.3，权重以 Apache 2.0 上架 Hugging Face，同时进入 OpenRouter 与自家 Decisions API，上下文 262,144 token。

核心参数与产品细节。

- 定位：决策模型介于大语言模型与专用分类器之间。请求提交一段状态（文本，可选图片）与若干命名问题，模型在一次前向中给出每个选项的概率分布，不做自回归生成。
- 支持题型：是或否、多选（每题最多 255 个选项）、有序打分；多个问题可共享同一段状态。
- 注意力结构：主干的全注意力层改为双向（非因果），团队试验了「全部可见」「问题隔离」「完全可缓存」三种模式，最终选择问题隔离，共享状态可见所有问题，每个问题只可见状态与自身 token，目的是让新增问题不改变已有答案。
- locate 功能：v1.3 新增的题型，输入字段名或自然语言指令，返回原文片段的起止字符位置与置信度，无匹配返回空列表；只支持纯文本，每请求最多 128 个 locate 问题，不能与联网检索同用；抽取头由独立 LoRA 适配器与 span head 组成，刻意不合并进主干，避免回退分类精度。
- 规模与许可：主模型基于 Qwen3.8-27B，BF16 权重约 49 GiB；Flash 基于 Qwen3.5-4B，约 8.5 GiB，由主模型以 KL 散度蒸馏得到，两者均为 Apache 2.0。
- 评测：63 项分类任务平均准确率 91.6%，比自家生产分类器高 6.54 个百分点；100 万条去标识化的真实请求上，与前沿模型判官的一致率 93.98%，v1.2 为 93.68%；17 项域外抽取任务平均 69.0 分，Flash 63.6 分。
- 定价：每百万输入 token 0.02 美元，Flash 0.01 美元，输出不计费，无按请求收费。
- 口径差异：模型卡正文写基于 Qwen3.8-27B，仓库头部标注 26B 参数，API 文档按 27B 计。

值得关注的原因。 把「判断题」从生成模型里拆出来，是过去一年推理成本优化里少见的架构级动作。路由、审核、打标、抽取这类任务占了企业调用量的很大一块，用聊天模型做等于为每个标签付一次长文本生成费用；决策模型一次前向出全部答案，还能把多个问题摊到同一段输入上。locate 的加入让它进一步侵入传统 NER 与信息抽取的地盘，抽出来的结果是原文的逐字切片，可回溯性强于生成式抽取。需要留意的限制同样明确：locate 不支持图片、不能与联网检索同用，抽取头是在最多 8,000 token 的输入上训练的；所有评测均为其自家 zero-shot 结果，公开榜单可被重复提交刷分的风险，Perplexity 自己在文档里也承认。

### 三、具身智能方向深度动态

#### 5. 曦选创智 5 亿元天使轮，芯片定义权写进股权结构

事件。 11 月 12 日，优必选披露其与沐曦股份联合发起的具身智能端侧芯片公司曦选创智完成 5 亿元人民币天使轮融资，投后估值 40 亿元，纪源资本与经纬创投联合领投，和利资本、鼎晖龙芯创投、上汽恒旭资本、耀途资本、正轩资本、心资本、优势资本、博雅创投等跟投。

核心参数与产品细节。

- 股权与人事：公司 2026 年 5 月成立，6 月 11 日在南京签约，注册资本 1 亿元；沐曦股份与优必选各持 35.01%，并列第一大股东，锋龙股份持 4.7%；沐曦创始人陈维良任董事长，优必选创始人周剑任副董事长，原新华三高级副总裁杨献波任 CEO。
- 产品目标：首颗自研芯片为国产 GPGPU 架构下的「大小脑一体」SoC，同时承担感知决策与运动控制，目标全面超过 NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor。
- 对标规格：Thor 公开数据为 2070 FP4 TFLOPS 算力、128GB 内存、40 至 130W 可调功耗，开发者套件发售价 3499 美元。
- 节奏：计划 2027 年下半年流片，2028 年量产；资金投向主控 SoC 研发、软件工具链、团队建设与样片到量产的工程化环节。
- 落地路径：端云协同，云侧 GPU 负责训练与高阶推理，端侧平台负责实时响应，运行记录与难题样本回流训练；验证用机器人由股东方提供，无锡规划的数据采集中心将部署数百台工业机器人。
- 市场格局：据 Yole Group，2025 年机器人 SoC 市场英伟达占 69%，中国厂商合计约 5%；同类玩家包括地瓜机器人（9 月 17 日 4 亿美元 C 轮，旭日 S600 标称 560 TOPS，旭日系列累计出货超 800 万片）、辉羲智能（10 月 28 日启动 A 股 IPO 辅导，R1 PRO 为 375 TOPS 大小脑融合芯片）、爱芯元智（具身大脑控制器标称 1500 TOPS）。

值得关注的原因。 这轮融资最值得看的是合资这种形态本身。供应合作与参考设计两种模式里，芯片定义权都不在本体厂商手里；合资意味着沐曦拿到真实机器人工作负载去反向定义一颗原生为具身设计的芯片，优必选则把对多模态感知与运动协同的理解写进架构，而不是等流片后再做适配。风险同样清晰：从 2026 年成立到 2028 年量产，中间要跨过流片、样片验证与车规级以外的机器人可靠性验证三轮，而这颗芯片的对手是一家已经迭代多年的产品线。股东结构决定了它至少有稳定的验证场景，但场景够不够多样，决定了这颗 SoC 是通用平台还是定制件。

#### 6. 优理奇完成 5 亿元 Pre-A，把出货量当作叙事核心

事件。 通用具身智能机器人公司优理奇机器人（UniX AI）宣布完成 5 亿元人民币 Pre-A 轮融资，老股东谢诺投资、涌铧投资连续多轮超额追加，新进投资方包括绿地集团、柯力传感、华工创投、新景富盈、红鸟启航基金、玉林产投等产业与财务投资人。

核心参数与产品细节。

- 公司背景：2023 年成立，总部北京，由前小米机器人团队核心成员创立。
- 产品线：Wanda 系列轮式人形机器人，搭载自研 UniBrain 具身大模型与多模态感知系统。
- 任务能力：在零售、餐饮、酒店、清洁等商业服务场景完成抓取、递送、制作饮品、整理货架等长时序任务。
- 交付数据：机器人稳定月出货超百台、峰值超 300 台；在京东七鲜咖啡落地 24 小时无人咖啡站，一台机器人连续制作 2156 杯饮品并创下吉尼斯世界纪录。
- 资金用途：深化具身智能算法研究与产品迭代，完善工程化交付体系，围绕物业、酒店、零售等既有场景推进规模化应用。

值得关注的原因。 具身智能公司的融资叙事正在从「模型多强」转向「交付多少台」。月出货百台量级意味着供应链、产线与售后已经跑通一轮，这是过去两年多数本体公司没有跨过的门槛；把单机连续 2156 杯这种极限工况公开，指向的是稳定性而非灵活性，与商业服务场景

DeepSeek.title: DeepSeek Put Its App Inside the API: Search, Files, Voice — and a Bill With Three Extra Lines
DeepSeek.description: On November 13, DeepSeek shipped a quiet but genuinely useful update in its API changelog: the search, link-reading, file-parsing, voice, and safety-checking capabilities that lived in the DeepSeek app are now callable directly from the API.
DeepSeek.content:
## DEV Community

On November 13, DeepSeek shipped a quiet but genuinely useful update in its API changelog: the search, link-reading, file-parsing, voice, and safety-checking capabilities that lived in the DeepSeek app are now callable directly from the API. No rebuilding the stack yourself.

The headline first: the update is not a new model. The model is still deepseek-flash (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017). What changed is how you call it — the "chat experience" has been broken down into billable building blocks.

## What actually opened up

Two layers.

The first layer is capabilities integrated into the conversation itself, available in the Messages, Responses, and Chat Completions APIs, switched on with parameters:

- Web search: thedeepseek_web_search tool. With thinking mode off, the model runs web or image search on demand and answers with citations. With thinking on, it can search and read links repeatedly across multiple reasoning rounds.
- Read URLs: thedeepseek_read_url tool pulls in links that appear in the message and reads them.
- File input: upload PDFs, Word docs, PPTs, and images; they are parsed into context before you ask. Parsing comes in two tiers — plain text extraction, or rich-layout recognition that preserves chart positions.
- Safety checks: asafety_check parameter that screens inputs and outputs, returning a refusal flag when something is risky.
- Auto titles and user-context metadata: the app's automatic conversation titles and context memory are in the API too.

The second layer is five standalone APIs, billed per call and not tied to a conversation: Search, Fetch, OCR, ASR, and TTS.

DeepSeek also open-sourced a demo chat client on GitHub, which can import your exported DeepSeek chat history — an official "copy this" reference implementation.

## The bill: three extra charges on top of tokens

The easiest mistake here is the pricing. Model tokens and tool calls are billed separately, and tool fees stack on top of token fees.

Capability | Price (DeepSeek pricing page, checked Nov 14) 
---|---
Search | $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests 
Fetch | $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests 
File parsing / OCR | $0.225 per 1,000 pages 
Speech-to-text (ASR) | 50% off for a limited time (no end date published) 
Text-to-speech (TTS) | $0.45 per 10,000 characters, $0.225 for a limited time 

The model itself, deepseek-flash: $0.30 input / $1.20 output per million tokens at peak hours, half price off-peak ($0.15 / $0.60).

A quick worked example: one conversation with 5 searches and a 10-page PDF parsed costs about 5 × $0.00075 + 10 × $0.000225 = $0.006 in tool fees — under a cent. Search is the line item that scales: if your agent searches dozens of times per conversation, tool fees can overtake token fees over a month. Test on small traffic first, then scale.

## A copy-paste call

Chat Completions API — turning on web search is one tool parameter:
{
  "model": "deepseek-flash",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "What changed in DeepSeek's November 13 API update?"}
  ],
  "tools": [
    {"type": "deepseek_web_search"}
  ]
}

Two details worth knowing. First, the built-in web tools require thinking mode to be off; with thinking on, the model takes a different multi-step search path, and the behavior is not the same — don't mix them up. Second, files go through a two-step upload-then-parse flow: you get a file_id first, then reference it in the conversation, and the parsing tier is chosen at upload time — it can't be changed later.

## Honest limitations: read these four before building

- Only deepseek-flash. The built-in web and file tools work on deepseek-flash only. deepseek-v4-pro can't use them — don't try it on Pro.
- The standalone Search/Fetch APIs are not new. They have existed since October 17. What's new this time is the in-conversation integration. Don't write this up as "DeepSeek launches search API for the first time."
- Tool fees are separate, and billed per successful request. Failed searches don't cost anything, but the definition of "successful" follows DeepSeek's billing page — check your invoice breakdown before going live.
- I haven't tested this hands-on. The facts above come from DeepSeek's official changelog and pricing page (checked November 14), cross-checked against two independent write-ups. Run the demo client end to end before putting it in production.

## Why this one is worth writing about

Three labs in the same week are all turning "capabilities" into billable building blocks: Google shipped its Decision 1 decision model on November 11, Anthropic moved Claude into the meeting room, and DeepSeek took its app apart into an API. The gap between models is narrowing; the gap is moving to whose blocks are cheaper and easier to snap together.

The yardstick for developers is changing too. It used to be benchmark scores. Now it's the total bill for one complete conversation. Search, parsing, and voice each have their own price list — only added together do they show the real cost.

Would you build your own chat client on this DeepSeek stack, or wait for a hosted version? Let me know in the comments.
